findings.claim: A retail assistant on £11.44 an hour (the 2024–25 UK minimum wage for those 21+) is on a wage.
findings.truth: £11.44 was the rate for April 2024 to March 2025. The rate for workers aged 21 and over is £12.21 from April 2025 and £12.71 from April 2026. A student revising for the 2027 exams would quote a figure two years out of date.
findings.evidence: gov.uk National Minimum Wage rates page (fetched 6 Sep 2026): 21 and over = £12.71 from 1 April 2026, £12.21 from April 2025.

findings.claim: the Partnership Council chose not to pay it in 2021, 2023 and 2024
findings.truth: The Partnership Council is a directly elected body of partners. It represents partners' opinions and holds the Chairman to account, and it is the only body that can remove the Chairman. It does not set or withhold the Partnership bonus; that sits with the Partnership Board. The years themselves are right, so the fix removes the wrong body rather than the dates.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, John Lewis Partnership (governance section) - Partnership Council role; no source attributes the bonus decision to the Council.

findings.claim: Examiners reward candidates who match the method to the specific business in the case study.
findings.truth: This is an invented claim about how examiners behave. The point is true as advice about application marks, so it should be stated as advice, not as a claim about examiner behaviour.
findings.evidence: House rule in the checker brief: fabricated examiner claims are a FIX. No board publishes this wording.

findings.claim: their working terms are set out in a contract of employment. UK law requires one to be issued on or before an employee's first day.
findings.truth: What must be given on or before day one is the written statement of employment particulars (Employment Rights Act 1996 s.1, as amended in April 2020). The contract itself can be oral. The lesson's version is the normal GCSE simplification and costs no marks.
findings.evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996 s.1 as amended (day-one right from 6 April 2020).

findings.claim: skills tests (a coding challenge at Dyson), presentations (marketing roles at Unilever), group tasks (graduate schemes at PwC)
findings.truth: The selection methods are all real and in scope. The company pairings are illustrative and are not sourced; Unilever's graduate selection is better known for digital and gamified assessments than for presentations. Nothing here is examinable, so no edit is made, but the named pairings should not be treated as verified.
findings.evidence: No source found within this session's fetch budget.

findings.claim: no bonus in 2021, 2023 and 2024 (also repeated in flashcard 10)
findings.truth: The list is correct as far as it goes, but it stops at 2024 and John Lewis has reported results twice since. The year list will need a refresh when the current results are confirmed. Not verified in this session, so no edit.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia confirms 2021 only; 2023 and 2024 match contemporaneous reporting.

summary: Three surgical fixes: a two-year-stale minimum wage figure, a John Lewis governance body named wrongly, and one fabricated examiner claim. All four calculation mark schemes were recomputed and are correct (40 divided by 3 = 13.33; £500; £46,000; £6,160), all 20 knowledge-check keys and all three match orders are right, no definition is reversed, and the unit makes no claim about papers, sections, timing or tariffs.
